description.narrative: Nordmakedonien befinner sig för närvarande i en mycket intensiv period när det gäller att slutföra EU:s granskningsprocess och skapa förutsättningar för beslutsfattande om politiskt känsliga ändringar i konstitutionen för att uppfylla villkoren för att inleda anslutningsförhandlingar. Det intensiva arbetet med EU-relaterade reformer fortsätter och dialogen med EU upprätthålls. Det stöd och flexibla tillvägagångssätt som Sverige gav till denna process med det föregående projektet (2018-2023) slutade med märkbara resultat i rättsliga reformer och kapacitetsuppbyggnad av EU-dialogen involverade personal. Detta stöd uppskattades mycket av sekretariatet för Europafrågor och de stödmottagande institutionerna. Den svenska ambassaden bedömer att det föreslagna projektet är relevant och lägligt mot bakgrund av det övergripande målet för regeringsprogrammet 2022-2024 och dess strategiska prioriteringar, samt enligt det nationella programmet för antagande av EU:s regelverk. Dess fokus på själva förhandlingsprocessen, kompletterad med antikorruption och kommunikationsdelen där det civila samhället och medierna deltar, är väl utformad och innehåller lärdomar från det föregående projektet och dess utvärdering. Med detta bidrag kommer Sverige att fortsätta att stödja kapacitetsuppbyggnad av relevant personal vid de institutioner som deltar i den EU-relaterade reformprocessen och EU-förhandlingarna, stärka den processrelaterade lagstiftningen, öka antikorruptionskapaciteten vid DPM:s kontor för god samhällsstyrning genom att tillhandahålla tekniskt bistånd och förbättra insynen i processen genom utbildning av journalister i EU-anslutningsprocessen. På grund av kommande val och möjlighet till regeringsskifte följt av eventuella ändrade prioriteringar på regeringens sida samt på EU-sidan planeras projektet att genomföras stegvis (fas I och fas II). I den första fasen kommer projektet att fortsätta att stödja strategisk miljöbedömning i den bilaterala granskningsprocessen, anpassningen av den nationella lagstiftningen till EU:s regelverk samt framstegen med de grundläggande reformerna genom tillhandahållande av högt specialiserat tekniskt bistånd. Det stegvisa tillvägagångssättet kommer att göra det möjligt att genomföra en översyn mot slutet av den första fasen som kommer att bedöma i) projektets framsteg ii) relevansen och genomförbarheten av de aktiviteter som för närvarande planeras för den andra fasen, samtidigt som regeringens åtagande och prioriteringar i samband med EU-integrationer beaktas. iii) Framsteg i verksamheten i samband med "överföring av äganderätt" till sekretariatet för Europafrågor, inklusive sekretariatet för Europafrågor som är redo att ta över mer genomförandeansvar. Översynen kommer därför att ligga till grund för införandet av justeringar av det eventuella stödet till fas II. En budget på 10 MSEK begärs för fas I, med genomförandetid på 20 månader.

North Macedonia presently is in a very intensive period finalizing the EU screening process and creating the conditions for decision making on politically sensitive changes in the Constitution in order to fulfill the conditions for initiating accession talks. Intensive work on EU related reforms continues, and dialogue is maintained with EU. The support and flexible approach provided by Sweden to this process with the predecessor project (2018-2023) ended with noticeable results in legal reform and capacity building of the EU dialogue involved staff. This support was highly appreciated by the Secretariat for European Affairs (now transformed into Ministry of European Affairs- MEA) and the benefiting institutions. The Swedish Embassy assesses the proposed project to be relevant and timely in light of the overall objective of the Governments Program 2022-2024 and its Strategic priorities, as well as according to the National Program for Adoption of the EU Acquis. Its focus on the negotiation process itself, complemented by anticorruption and communication part in which civil society and media are involved, is well-designed and incorporates lessons learned from the predecessor project and its evaluation. With this contribution Sweden will continue supporting capacity building of relevant staff in the institutions that are involved in the EU related reform process and EU negotiations, strengthen the process related legislation, increase anti-corruption capacity of the office of DPM for Good Governance by providing technical assistance , and improve transparency of the process by training of journalists in the EU accession process. Due to upcoming elections and possibility for change of Government followed by possible change in priorities on the side of the Government as well on the EU side, the project is planned to be implemented with phased approach (Phase I and Phase II). In the first phase, the Project will continue to support MEA in the bilateral screening process, alignment of the national legislation with the EU acquis as well as the progress on the fundamental reforms through the provision of highly specialized technical assistance. The phased approach will allow for the conduct of a review towards the end of the first phase that will assess: i) the Project’s progress ii) relevance and feasibility of the activities currently planned for the second phase, while also considering Government's commitment and priorities related to EU integrations. iii) progress of activities related to “Transfer of Ownership” to Ministry for European Affairs, including Ministry for European Affairs readiness to take over more implementation responsibilities. The Review will therefore provide basis for the introduction of adjustments in the possible support of Phase II. A budget of 10mSEK is requested for Phase I, with implementation period of 20 months.

The phased approach for the contribution for Support to EU integration to North Macedonia (Phase I- 1 September 2023- 31 October 2024 and Phase II - 1st November 2024 - 31st October 2027) enabled a comprehensive project review towards the end of the first project phase, which assessed: (i) the projects overall progress, and (ii) the relevance and feasibility of the activities planned for the second phase. The review also took into account the Governments commitment and priorities regarding EU integration, including MEAs readiness to assume greater project implementation responsibilities. Based on this review, adjustments were introduced to the second phase of the project in sense of strengthened approach in some activities where the growing demand and need for support was emerging. For Phase II, support under the Project does not include provision of legal advice or drafting, development, or revision of legislation, nor the preparation of any legal , or judicial documents or tools. This scope limitation is intended to avoid overlap and potential double funding of assistance already provided through EU-funded interventions.
The overall objective of the Swedish support is to contribute to the efficient and effective EU integration process and to overall management of EU integration of North Macedonia. It directly contributes to conducting of screenings and finalization of reports for clusters, while in particular facilitating opening of Fundamentals Cluster and fulfilment of requirements deriving from it.
The Specific project objective are:
- to enhance institutional, technical, and administrative capacity of the Government of North Macedonia to conduct EU accession, and
- to facilitate engagement of the civil society, academia, youth, media, and public in the EU integration process.
The project aims to achieve the following results:
Result 1: Capacities of National Institutions Supporting EU Accession Negotiations and Integration Strengthened
The Project provides targeted support to strengthen the Government's coordination mechanisms for EU accession negotiations through technical assistance to the Ministry of European Affairs (MEA), line ministries, and negotiation structures. It supports key inter-institutional bodies, including the Working Committee for European Integration (WCEI), NPAA Working Groups, and Reform Agenda coordination structures.
The Project also assists Parliament in monitoring the EU accession process, with particular support provided to the Committee for European Affairs (CEA) and the National Council for European Integration (NCEI).
Regional cooperation is reinforced through expert exchanges with EU Member States from the region, while tailored capacity-building programs support the implementation of the Reform Agenda, the National Programme for the Adoption of the Acquis (NPAA), and European Commission recommendations. These efforts contribute to strengthening North Macedonia's institutional preparedness for EU accession.
Result 2: Professional and Technical Capacities of the Ministry of European Affairs Strengthened
The Project strengthens the professional and technical capacities of the Ministry of European Affairs by enhancing its training and knowledge-management functions. It supports the translation of key strategic documents in line with EU standards and provides recommendations for establishing a coordination framework aimed at harmonizing EU-related terminology.
A particular focus has been placed on strengthening the MEA Training Centre. Training needs assessments guide the design of targeted learning programs, including online courses, upgraded training facilities, digital learning tools, and specialized training materials. These interventions contribute to the establishment of a sustainable and institutionalized training system for stakeholders involved in the EU accession process.
Result 3: Capacities and Coordination Role for Good Governance and Anti-Corruption Policies Strengthened
The Project strengthened capacities for coordinating good governance and anti-corruption reforms by supporting the mainstreaming of anti-corruption measures across relevant negotiation chapters, promoting the principle that no chapter should be provisionally closed without adequate anti-corruption safeguards.
Through the engagement of experts from EU Member States and the region, the Project enhanced institutional capacities to coordinate anti-corruption reforms, support negotiation positions, and promote integrity, transparency, and good governance standards. It also contributed to the identification of corruption-prone areas, improved inter-institutional coordination, and supported the development of procedures for more efficient decision-making.
In addition, the Project developed a road-map for establishing an Anti-Corruption Observatory, aligned with EU best practices and the Negotiating Framework. The Observatory is envisaged as a mechanism for monitoring corruption cases, analyzing law-enforcement data, and assessing the effectiveness and impact of anti-corruption policies.
However, the Government's recent decision, effective from 13 July 2026, to abolish the position of Deputy Prime Minister for Good Governance and transfer the related coordination responsibilities to the Office of the Prime Minister has implications to the Project. The Deputy Prime Minister for Good Governance was a key institutional stakeholder and the designated focal point for coordinating the Project's anti-corruption activities. At the same time, should the Office of the Prime Minister assume direct responsibility for coordinating anti-corruption reforms, this change of authority may also present an opportunity. It could elevate the priority of anti-corruption reforms, strengthen political ownership, accelerate decision-making processes, and improve coordination across ministries and public institutions.
Result 4: Public Awareness of the EU Accession Process and Its Impact Increased
The Project supports MEA in strengthening and structuring its communication efforts to enhance public understanding of the EU accession process and its benefits. Through community dialogues, public debates, round-tables, and town hall meetings, the Project promotes transparency, stimulates informed public discussion, and stakeholder engagement at both national and local levels.
To further broaden outreach and public participation, the Project successfully launched the Call for Proposals Strengthening Public Engagement and Communication on the Road to EU Membership, designed to enhance public understanding, participation, and oversight of the EU accession process through targeted support to Parliament, media, civil society, and youth organisations.
The Project also places strong emphasis on youth engagement. Partnerships for students and youth engagement in European integrations is supported though the grant funding for youth organisations, debates, competitions, public lectures, internship opportunities, and other educational initiatives.
Collectively, these interventions aim to empower civil society, strengthen independent media, foster informed public discourse, and ensure a more inclusive and participatory dialogue on North Macedonia's EU integration process.
Since April 2024, the Government of Switzerland has complemented the support provided by Sweden and the MEA through additional assistance aimed at strengthening the capacity of Parliament to effectively contribute to and oversee the EU accession process. This support is highly complementary and builds on the institutional strengthening efforts supported by Sweden. In addition, Switzerland provides technical assistance to the EU integration process in the area of Environment and Climate Change (Chapter 27), further reinforcing national capacities in critical accession-related sectors (budget line 5.1.3).
